kept.claim: TopicUser.find_by returns nil when the logged-in user has no topic_users row for the topic, so tu.notification_level raises NoMethodError and the unsubscribe link returns a 500.
kept.body:
## [ISSUE] `unsubscribe` crashes with NoMethodError when no TopicUser row exists

**Severity:** HIGH — the unsubscribe link returns HTTP 500 instead of unsubscribing

### The Problem

```ruby
tu = TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])

if tu.notification_level > TopicUser.notification_levels[:regular]
```

`find_by` returns `nil` when there is no row, and nothing checks for that before `tu.notification_level` is called.

### Theory / Proof

- `ensure_logged_in` only checks that *some* user is logged in. The URL (`Topic#unsubscribe_url`) holds nothing tied to the recipient, so it works the same for any logged-in account.
- `TopicView.new(params[:topic_id], current_user)` only checks that the user can see the topic. It does not create a `topic_users` row.
- `TopicUser` rows are created lazily, by `TopicUser.change` / `track_visit!` / `update_last_read`. A user who can see a topic but never visited it and was never emailed about it has no row.

### What happens today vs. what will break

The row usually exists for the email recipient, because `UserNotifications#send_notification_email` calls `TopicUser.change(... last_emailed_post_number:)`. It breaks when:
- the email is forwarded or opened in a browser that is logged in as a different account (shared or family computer, admin impersonation);
- someone opens `/t/slug/123/unsubscribe` directly for a topic they have never visited;
- the row was removed, for example by user merge or topic move.

Each of these gives `NoMethodError: undefined method 'notification_level' for nil:NilClass` and a 500 page.

### Research

The existing mute/notification endpoints in this controller (`set_notifications`, `mute`) go through `TopicUser.change`, which upserts. They never assume the row exists.

### Recommendation

Use the upsert helper and default to `regular` when there is no row:

```ruby
tu = TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: @topic_view.topic.id)
current = tu ? tu.notification_level : TopicUser.notification_levels[:regular]
new_level = current > TopicUser.notification_levels[:regular] ?
  TopicUser.notification_levels[:regular] : TopicUser.notification_levels[:muted]
TopicUser.change(current_user.id, @topic_view.topic.id, notification_level: new_level)
```
kept.evidence: topics_controller.rb:105 find_by can return nil; :107 dereferences without a nil check. ensure_logged_in and TopicView.new (lib/topic_view.rb:31-72) never create a TopicUser row. The link has no per-recipient token, so any logged-in user who has never visited the topic, or who opens a forwarded link, gets NoMethodError / 500. Recipients usually have a row because user_notifications.rb calls TopicUser.change before sending.

kept.claim: tu.save! bypasses TopicUser.change, so notifications_reason_id stays NULL and the auto-track SQL in TopicUser.update_last_read silently flips the level back to tracking on the next read; no MessageBus notification_level_change is published either.
kept.body:
## [ISSUE] Unsubscribe is silently undone by auto-tracking because `save!` skips `TopicUser.change`

**Severity:** MEDIUM — users who unsubscribe start getting notifications again

### The Problem

```ruby
tu.notification_level = TopicUser.notification_levels[:regular]  # or :muted
tu.save!
```

This writes only `notification_level`. `TopicUser.change` (app/models/topic_user.rb:77-114) does two more things whenever the level changes:

```ruby
attrs[:notifications_changed_at] ||= DateTime.now
attrs[:notifications_reason_id] ||= TopicUser.notification_reasons[:user_changed]
...
MessageBus.publish("/topic/#{topic_id}", { notification_level_change: ... }, user_ids: [user_id])
```

### Theory / Proof

`TopicUser.update_last_read` (app/models/topic_user.rb ~160) re-computes the level every time timings are posted:

```sql
notification_level =
  case when tu.notifications_reason_id is null and (tu.total_msecs_viewed + :msecs) >
       coalesce(u.auto_track_topics_after_msecs,:threshold) ... then :tracking
  else tu.notification_level end
```

The CASE does not look at the current level. It only needs `notifications_reason_id IS NULL`. That is exactly the state of:
- auto-tracked rows (this same SQL promotes them without setting a reason), and
- rows created by `TopicUser.change(last_emailed_post_number: ...)` when an email is sent.

Both are common among users who get notification emails, and `save!` leaves the reason NULL.

### What happens today vs. what will break

1. A user was auto-tracked (reason NULL, level `tracking`) and gets an email.
2. They click "click here": the level becomes `regular`, and the reason is still NULL.
3. The next time they read that topic (with `total_msecs_viewed` already above the threshold), `update_last_read` sets the level back to `tracking` and publishes the change.

The unsubscribe is undone without the user doing anything. The same path takes a `muted` user back to `tracking`. Also, other open tabs never get the `notification_level_change` MessageBus event, so their notification button shows the old level.

### Research

All other notification-level writes in this codebase (`TopicsController#set_notifications`, `#mute`, `CategoryUser` auto-watch) go through `TopicUser.change` for exactly this reason. The reason id is what stops later auto-tracking from overriding the user's choice.

### Recommendation

```ruby
TopicUser.change(current_user.id, @topic_view.topic.id, notification_level: new_level)
```

This sets `notifications_reason_id = user_changed`, stamps `notifications_changed_at` and publishes the MessageBus update.
kept.evidence: save! skips TopicUser.change (topic_user.rb:77-117), which sets notifications_reason_id=user_changed and publishes the MessageBus notification_level_change. The update_last_read SQL (topic_user.rb:153-179) sets the level to tracking whenever reason_id IS NULL and the view time is above the threshold, whatever the current level. Auto-tracked rows and rows created by track_visit! have a NULL reason. set_notifications (topics_controller.rb:332) uses TopicUser.change.

kept.claim: The unsubscribe endpoint changes the notification level on a plain GET, and the new level depends on the current one, so it is not idempotent: reloading the page, or any repeat or cross-site GET of the URL, lowers the level again (for example regular -> muted) without the user choosing it.
kept.body:
## [ISSUE] State-changing, non-idempotent GET: reloading the unsubscribe page lowers the level again

**Severity:** MEDIUM — a reload, or any repeat or cross-site GET, changes the user's notification level without them choosing it

### The Problem

```ruby
get "t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe" => "topics#unsubscribe"
...
if tu.notification_level > TopicUser.notification_levels[:regular]
  tu.notification_level = TopicUser.notification_levels[:regular]
else
  tu.notification_level = TopicUser.notification_levels[:muted]
end
tu.save!
perform_show_response
```

Each GET lowers the level by one step from whatever it currently is, then renders the HTML page (`perform_show_response` now calls `render :show`).

### Theory / Proof

- RFC 7231 §4.2.1/§4.2.2: GET is expected to be safe and idempotent. Browsers re-issue it on reload, session restore, and "reopen closed tab". Here each re-issue runs the action again. A user who clicked the link at `tracking`/`watching` and lands on `regular` is dropped to `muted` by a single reload of the confirmation page.
- `protect_from_forgery` (application_controller.rb:21) does not check GET, and `ensure_logged_in` only needs the session cookie. A third-party page can send a logged-in user to `https://forum/t/x/123/unsubscribe` (a top-level navigation) and change their notification level for that topic.

Client-side Ember navigation does not re-trigger this. `routes/topic-unsubscribe.js.es6` loads data through `PostStream.loadTopicView`, not the unsubscribe URL. Only real HTTP GETs are affected.

### Research

RFC 8058 (one-click List-Unsubscribe) requires the unsubscribe action to be a POST for this reason. Discourse's digest unsubscribe (`EmailController#unsubscribe`) shows a page and changes state on POST.

### Recommendation

Render on GET and change state on POST. If GET must change state, make it idempotent by setting a fixed target level:

```ruby
TopicUser.change(current_user.id, @topic_view.topic.id,
                 notification_level: TopicUser.notification_levels[:muted])
```
kept.evidence: The level changes on a GET (routes.rb, topics_controller.rb:98-116), and the new level depends on the current one. perform_show_response renders HTML, so a reload runs the action again (regular -> muted). protect_from_forgery does not check GET, so a cross-site navigation can trigger it. The one-step watching -> regular change is deliberate, and the page shows topic-notifications-button so the user can pick a level. The 'bug for watching users' part is overstated.

kept.claim: The new TopicsController#unsubscribe endpoint and the unsubscribe_url interpolation in emails have no tests; the only spec change passes unsubscribe_url without asserting it appears in the output.
kept.body:
## [GAP ANALYSIS] New unsubscribe endpoint has no controller specs

**Severity:** LOW — the nil-row crash and level-transition bugs above would have been caught by tests

### The Problem

The PR adds `TopicsController#unsubscribe`, two routes and a new interpolation (`%{unsubscribe_url}`) in the `unsubscribe_link` email string. The only spec change is in `spec/components/email/message_builder_spec.rb`, where `unsubscribe_url: "/t/1234/unsubscribe"` is added to the builder options so interpolation does not fail. Nothing checks that the URL appears in the body or HTML part. `spec/controllers/topics_controller_spec.rb` has no tests for `unsubscribe`.

### Theory / Proof

These untested paths hold the logic most likely to break:
- the anonymous-user case (`ensure_logged_in`);
- no `TopicUser` row (currently `NoMethodError`);
- watching -> regular, and regular -> muted;
- slug mismatch -> 301 to `unsubscribe_url`.

### Recommendation

```ruby
describe 'unsubscribe' do
  let(:topic) { Fabricate(:topic) }
  let!(:user) { log_in }

  it 'mutes a regular topic' do
    TopicUser.change(user.id, topic.id, notification_level: TopicUser.notification_levels[:regular])
    xhr :get, :unsubscribe, topic_id: topic.id, slug: topic.slug
    expect(TopicUser.get(topic, user).notification_level).to eq(TopicUser.notification_levels[:muted])
  end

  it 'does not error when no TopicUser row exists' do
    xhr :get, :unsubscribe, topic_id: topic.id, slug: topic.slug
    expect(response).to be_success
  end
end
```

Also assert in message_builder_spec that `message_with_unsubscribe.body` includes `/t/1234/unsubscribe`.
kept.evidence: spec/controllers/topics_controller_spec.rb has no unsubscribe tests. message_builder_spec.rb:168-179 passes unsubscribe_url but never asserts that it appears in the output.
